exposure: Type I: Invasion of skin and subcutaneous tissue
Type II: Invasion of fascia and rectus abdominis
cohort: This study included 367 patients who underwent resection of abdominal-wall endometriotic lesions at the Peking Union Medical College Hospital between January 2008 and December 2018.
finding: Type III AWE presents with more severe clinical features, larger lesion size, increased operative time and surgical difficulty, higher mesh implantation necessity, and prolonged postoperative recovery.
